item.title: ProAC / Fomento CultSP: Edital 05/2026, Electronic Games Development and Publishing
item.description:
Organisation: Secretaria da Cultura, Economia e Industria Criativas do Estado de Sao Paulo (ProAC)

Location: Sao Paulo state, Brazil. Open only to legal entities headquartered in Sao Paulo state for at least two years.

Award: BRL 300,000 (around USD 55,000 / EUR 50,000) per selected project, 20 projects total across two modules, from a BRL 6,000,000 pool. Registration is free.

Duration: Module I funds game development; Module II funds finalisation and publishing of an existing game.

Deadline: 27 Jul 2026

Sao Paulo state's ProAC scheme runs one of the largest dedicated public funds for game development in Latin America. Edital 05/2026 splits BRL 6,000,000 across two modules of ten projects each: Module I for developing electronic games, Module II for finalising and publishing them, at BRL 300,000 per project. At least six of the ten slots in each module are reserved for applicants based outside the state capital. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED AND NARROW: individuals cannot apply. Applicants must be legal entities, meaning private companies (for-profit or not-for-profit) or registered MEI microentrepreneurs, headquartered in Sao Paulo state for at least two years, with artistic or cultural activity expressly stated in their founding documents. Applications close 27 July 2026 at 23:59:59 Brasilia time via fomento.sp.gov.br. Note this is a tight deadline.

item.title: POM Fukuoka 2027: Politics of the Machines, Call for Abstracts
item.description:
Organisation: POM (Politics of the Machines) Conference, hosted at Kyushu University Ohashi Campus

Location: Fukuoka, Japan (Kyushu University Ohashi Campus, in person)

Award: Unpaid, and self-funded. POM explicitly cannot provide financial support for travel, accommodation, registration or other participation costs, and authors of accepted abstracts must register for the conference in order to present. No abstract submission fee.

Duration: Conference in 2027; accepted authors are later invited to submit a full paper of up to 4,000 words

Deadline: 30 Aug 2026

Call for abstracts for the POM (Politics of the Machines) conference in Fukuoka, hosted on Kyushu University's Ohashi Campus, organised around the theme of transduction. TRACKS: 01 The Landscape of Transduction: Infrastructural Entanglements of Energy, Data, and More-than-Human Life; 02 Parasitic Transductions Beyond the Human; 03 Real Machines: Computation, Subjectivity, and the Politics of Reality-Production; 04 Technogenetic Transductions across Fields of Experience: Affective Politics in/for Times of Crisis; 05 Transducing Disgust: Bodies, Technologies, and the Synthetic Uncanny; 06 Methoding Transduction: Sound, Data, Sonic Research; 07 Metabolic Worldviews and Hybrid Intelligences; 08 Fermentative Systems; 09 Unhearing Bodies: Life as Transduction; and 10, an open track for Speculations and Culturing Immature Ideas. FORMATS: academic papers, lecture-performances, artistic interventions and workshops, with proposals for alternative formats also encouraged; indicate the intended format in the submission. FACILITIES: beyond the Multi Purpose Building and Design Library, the campus offers a BioFoodLab (a Biolab and a Foodlab, each holding roughly 20 people) and an Acoustic Research Center (recording studio for up to 50, anechoic chamber for up to 15, echo chamber / reverberation room for up to 10, and semi-anechoic chamber for up to 20), which the organisers flag as relevant to tracks engaging sound, food, perception, signal and technological mediation. SUBMIT: an abstract of up to 500 words under one of the tracks; submissions without a track will be assigned to the most appropriate one. All submissions go through double-blind peer review, and authors of accepted abstracts are invited to present. The submission platform is described as opening soon. AFTER: accepted authors are invited to submit a full paper of up to 4,000 words including references, with a formal call for papers to follow. COSTS: note that this is a self-funded opportunity. Presenting requires paid conference registration, and POM cannot cover travel, accommodation, registration or other participation expenses. DEADLINE: 30 August 2026.

item.title: Building Narrative Power: EUR 2m funding and learning programme
item.description:
Organisation: European AI & Society Fund

Location: Europe (organisations across Europe)

Award: Grants of up to EUR 150,000 from a EUR 2 million programme, plus participation in a learning programme and community of practice. No application fee.

Duration: Project grant with an accompanying learning programme

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

The European AI & Society Fund is launching Building Narrative Power, a EUR 2 million funding and learning programme to counter Big Tech's dominance over how AI is understood, and to help people and communities shape new ways of thinking and talking about the technology they want. The Fund's strategy is to build the power of the public interest community to shape the direction of AI in Europe; narratives are central to creating the conditions for a greater say over how AI is adopted and used. THREE THEMES where research shows the public already feels strongly: (1) DATA CENTRES: as the EU aims to triple data centre numbers in the next five to seven years, pollution, energy prices and compromised grid access have mobilised communities across the political spectrum; proposals should explore narrative questions that move communities beyond resistance towards engagement in shaping data centre expansion. (2) AI AND JOBS: 57% of the public in a recent study expressed concern about how AI will change employment, more pronounced among lower-income people, and the concern is not only displacement but the quality and nature of work, autonomy and dignity; proposals should move the debate from generalised anxiety into a mobilising issue that shapes the future of work. (3) YOUNG PEOPLE: beyond the strident social media ban debate, young people encounter AI in education, friendships and future careers, and their wider views are rarely heard; proposals should build narratives that help young people shape the technologies that will influence their lives. LEARNING PROGRAMME: grantees join a community of practice, sharing experiences across issues and places, supporting each other through delivery and reflecting on which strategies and stories have most salience, with findings feeding back to the Fund and other funders. Deadline for first-stage applications is 31 August 2026.

item.title: KHN Center for the Arts: Artist Residency
item.description:
Organisation: Kimmel Harding Nelson Center for the Arts

Location: Nebraska City, Nebraska, United States. Open internationally.

Award: USD 175/week stipend, plus free living and studio space. $35 application fee, collected via the SlideRoom application portal.

Duration: Residencies of 2-8 weeks; applications reviewed in two annual cycles (1 March and 1 September). The 2027 1st Session covers awards scheduled 4 January to 25 June 2027.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

The Kimmel Harding Nelson Center for the Arts (KHN) in Nebraska City supports established and emerging writers, visual artists, and composers/musicians by providing living and studio space that allows uninterrupted time for work, reflection, and creative growth. Residencies run 2 to 8 weeks and include free living and studio space plus a USD 175/week stipend. KHN awards approximately 30-38 residencies per session, of which roughly 8-12 go to visual artists working in various media. Categories: Writers & Poets, Visual Artists, Composers & Musicians, and Interdisciplinary Artists. Visual artists work in one of three studios (two approximately 425 sq ft and one 258 sq ft) outfitted with work tables, running water, and storage shelves; donated hand tools, a bandsaw, miter saw, and painting easels are available. Upon request, artists with previous printing experience may access the onsite Harry Duncan Letterpress Studio (SP15 Vandercook Proof Press, a 16x12 inch boxcar base for adhesive plates, furniture, fonts, and a small inventory of printmaking tools). Open internationally. Applications are reviewed twice a year (deadlines 1 March and 1 September); the 2027 1st Session (deadline 1 September 2026) is for awards scheduled 4 January to 25 June 2027. All applications must be submitted online via SlideRoom; mailed or emailed applications are not considered. A $35 application fee is collected through the portal.

item.title: BFI National Lottery Discovery Feature Funding (Debut Fiction Features)
item.description:
Organisation: British Film Institute (BFI Filmmaking Fund, National Lottery)

Location: United Kingdom (applications must come from a limited company registered and centrally managed in the UK)

Award: Up to GBP 1,000,000 of National Lottery funding towards a fiction feature with a production budget between GBP 1,000,000 and GBP 3,500,000. No application fee.

Duration: Single production award; apply at least 20 weeks before the first day of principal photography. Decisions in principle within roughly 12 weeks of the round closing.

Deadline: 13 Aug 2026

Discovery is the debut-director production strand of the BFI Filmmaking Fund, awarding up to GBP 1 million towards fiction features budgeted between GBP 1 million and GBP 3.5 million. It backs first-time feature directors working alongside experienced producers, and is structured so creative risk sits with a team rather than a lone filmmaker. ELIGIBILITY: applications must be made through a limited company registered and centrally managed in the UK, so unincorporated individuals cannot apply. A dedicated lead producer with an established track record must submit, and that producer must be someone other than the writer or director. The director must be making their first fiction feature, meaning no prior feature at or above a GBP 1 million budget and no prior commercial UK or Ireland theatrical distribution of a fiction feature. At least two people must be credited across the writer, producer and director roles, all aged 18 or over and not in full-time education. Projects need a fully developed script and a runtime of at least 70 minutes. LIMITS: one application per production company, producer and director per round, and applications must arrive at least 20 weeks before the proposed first day of principal photography. ROUNDS: Round 2 closes at 5pm on Thursday 13 August 2026. Round 3 opens Thursday 12 November 2026 and closes Wednesday 16 December 2026. Successful applicants must publicly credit BFI National Lottery support.

item.title: Project Liberty: Co-Lab Fund Micro-Grants (Round 2, 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Project Liberty (Alliance SteerCo); pooled fund supported by Future of Life Institute, Omidyar Network, Ergo Impact, and Project Liberty

Location: Members of the Project Liberty coalition (Alliance). Projects led by a Coalition member organization; geography otherwise unrestricted.

Award: Micro-grants of USD 10,000 or less, a deliberate change from Round 1's larger awards so the Fund reaches more of the Coalition. Preference given to organizations that did not receive a Round 1 award. No application fee.

Duration: Short, discrete projects. Applicants must be ready to begin substantive work within two weeks of approval. This is the final round of the summer; the Fund is expected to resume later in 2026.

Deadline: 29 Jul 2026

MEMBERS ONLY: this is a member-led collaboration fund, not an open public call. Projects must be led by a Project Liberty Coalition (Alliance) member organization. Round 2 shifts to micro-grants of USD 10,000 or less, an iterative change from Round 1 intended to spread support across more of the Coalition; organizations that did not receive a Round 1 award are preferred. SCOPE: micro-grants fund two kinds of work, (1) discrete projects that strengthen the Coalition itself, such as Shared Services or convenings, and (2) time-sensitive collaborative projects within a designated workstream. In both cases the work should begin quickly and produce something concrete. A STRONG APPLICATION SHOWS: work that builds the Coalition as an entity, such as shared tools, infrastructure or connections that make joint action easier; clear alignment with a Coalition workstream; value for multiple Coalition organizations; a strong case that the work would not happen, or would move more slowly, without the Fund; a concrete outcome such as a tool, resource, convening, campaign or research product; and readiness to begin substantive work within two weeks of approval. LIMIT: one application per organization, submitted through the existing Co-Lab Fund application form. Round 1 results were still pending at the time of this call, with funded projects to be shared soon and engagement opportunities expected across the work. Prospective applicants unsure whether an idea fits this round are invited to reach out first. DEADLINE: 29 July 2026 at midnight. Background on the Co-Lab program is in the Coalition's overview document.

item.title: Antikythera Journal: Agentworld Special Issue, Call for Papers
item.description:
Organisation: Antikythera (Antikythera: Journal for the Philosophy of Planetary Computation, published with MIT Press)

Location: Remote (online submission; the journal is web-first and design-forward)

Award: Unpaid. No honorarium or fee is offered for accepted contributions; the return is peer-reviewed publication in the MIT Press-published Antikythera Journal. No submission fee.

Duration: Single publication; first selection of articles published Fall 2026

Deadline: 20 Aug 2026

Antikythera, a research programme on planetary computation and the evolution of intelligence, invites contributions to Agentworld, a special issue of its peer-reviewed MIT Press journal launching Fall 2026. THEME: Agentworld is a research initiative on the medium-term future of hybrid human-AI societies, framed not around tools for agentic task completion but around what the brief calls 'the human perplexity of deep agentic diffusion'. It treats human societies as the evolutionary niches into which new artificial species must adapt, where the constraints of agentic integration are qualitative and open-ended (psychological, philosophical, linguistic, symbolic, existential) rather than utility functions to be solved. The framing describes a 'parasociety' of densely reticulated social graphs in which agent-to-agent communication constitutes most socially significant interaction, humans and agents anthropomorphise each other by inheritance rather than necessity, and the two overlapping societies act as mutual evolutionary niches. The disciplinary posture proposed is 'a preemptive anthropology of open-world centaur societies': building the vocabulary, scenarios and conceptual armature for an emergent sociality while it is still forming, rather than describing it after the fact. WHAT THEY WANT: theoretical essays and technical papers that engage the Agentworld themes directly and explain how the contribution adds to the special issue's core questions. Philosophical, theoretical, technical, design-led and product-oriented research are all in scope. The call explicitly favours work that exceeds conventional academic journal formats, including contributions combining philosophical argument, technical analysis, design research, diagrams, software, infrastructure proposals, visual media or web-native formats. Contributors may optionally propose still images, diagrams, video, web-based or interactive components, and should say whether they have the design, development or production capacity to realise them; these elements are not required. SUBMIT: an abstract or proposal of up to 500 words; author name(s), affiliation(s), contact details, biography(ies) and CV(s); a designated lead author or contact person for collaborative submissions; and a portfolio with at least one relevant work sample such as a preprint, published article or paper. Full paper drafts are encouraged where available but not required at the initial stage. Submissions may be individual or collaborative. TIMING: the review window opened 25 June 2026. NOTE: no closing date is published on the call page; the deadline shown here is a placeholder set roughly a month out, so check the site or submit early.

item.title: The Gallery at Penn College: 2027-28 Call for Exhibitions
item.description:
Organisation: The Gallery at Penn College (Pennsylvania College of Technology)

Location: Williamsport, Pennsylvania, United States (campus of Pennsylvania College of Technology). Williamsport Regional Airport connects to Washington-Dulles; no other direct flights or trains.

Award: Housing, meals, a solo exhibition honorarium, and a shipping and travel stipend are provided. No application fee.

Duration: Exhibitions scheduled during the 2027-28 season. Jurying takes place in the Fall 2026 semester; artists are notified in January 2027.

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

The Gallery at Penn College (Pennsylvania College of Technology, Williamsport, PA) invites artists to apply for solo, two-person, or group exhibitions for its 2027-28 season. All entries are juried through a blind selection process by a gallery committee of faculty, staff, K-12 art educators, and community artists; review takes place during the Fall semester and artists receive notification in January. PROVIDED: housing, meals, a solo exhibition honorarium, and a shipping and travel stipend. Promotional support includes an annual gallery catalog, postcards, press releases, and web and social media. THE SPACE: the Gallery is 3,000 square feet with 82-250 running feet of linear wall space and an 11'4" ceiling. All exhibitions are installed by Gallery staff; site-specific installations requiring artist installation need a planning document approved before scheduling. Artists must have enough work for a solo exhibition unless applying for a two-person show. ENGAGEMENT: campus visits are an important part of programming (some exhibitions are scheduled without a visit). Penn College offers a B.S. in Graphic Design with foundation courses in drawing, 2D and 3D design, visual literacy, painting, ceramics, wood sculpture, printmaking, and computer graphics; artists are encouraged to propose class-specific programs and optional community workshops. Visiting artists give a 20-30 minute gallery talk during the public reception (held Tuesdays through Thursdays). TO APPLY: 10-15 digital images of work (JPG/JPEG only, max 4 MB each), an image list with dimensions and medium, a CV, and an artist statement. For two-person or group proposals, provide details in the comments; for video work, upload a PDF with video links and details. Deadline 31 August 2026 for the 2027-28 season.

The Institute for Advanced Study is seeking a 2026-27 Civic Science Fellow to advance understanding of the social, democratic and scientific implications of artificial intelligence. The remaining 25% supports the Fellow's own independent research, network-building and full participation in the intellectual life of IAS. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: a PhD in the social sciences, sciences or humanities; a strong record of scholarly research, writing and publication on the social implications of science and technology or related fields; and exceptional writing and editing skills for both academic and non-academic audiences. Preferred: specialization in science and technology studies, science and technology policy, organizational studies or qualitative methods, and demonstrated engagement with AI governance and technology policy debates. DigiPulse is a three-year longitudinal, international research project in LSE's Digital Futures for Children centre investigating the real-time relationships between children's smartphone use and their wellbeing, with data collected in the UK, Brazil and Kenya. The project combines passive smartphone tracking, Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) and longitudinal surveys with around 750 children and young people aged 10-17. THE ROLE: the Research Officer plays a central part in project management, development, data collection and analysis, with particular responsibility for developing and refining EMA instruments, contributing to the research literature and hypotheses, supporting participatory and consultative work with children, and conducting statistical analysis and producing findings, working closely with partners in the UK, Brazil and Kenya. Award: $4,000 stipend for two-month terms or $1,000 for two-week terms, to assist with living expenses and supplies, plus solo live-in accommodation and studio at the historic James Castle House. Residents donate one selected piece to the City of Boise collection at the end of the term. No application fee.

Duration: Two-month terms (1 Mar - 30 Apr, 1 Jun - 31 Jul, 1 Sep - 31 Oct 2027) or two-week terms (11-25 Jan and 1-15 Dec 2027)

Deadline: 28 Aug 2026

The James Castle House in Boise, Idaho (the preserved home of self-taught artist James Castle) opens applications for its 2027 residency terms from 16 July to 28 August 2026. TWO-MONTH RESIDENCY: an immersive focus on a project or body of work responding to the history and legacy of James Castle or the site; open to artists, scholars, creators and professionals in any field; $4,000 stipend; residents share their practice through public events (workshops, open studios, presentations) and donate a selected piece to the City of Boise collection. Terms: 1 March - 30 April, 1 June - 31 July, or 1 September - 31 October 2027. TWO-WEEK RESIDENCY: time and space for a single site-responsive project; $1,000 stipend; one public event. Terms: 11-25 January or 1-15 December 2027. A rolling PROJECT RESIDENCY also considers proposals case by case (email jamescastlehouse@cityofboise.org). ELIGIBILITY: 18+, legally able to work in the United States, able to pass a background check; emerging and mid-career practitioners in any field, though the property cannot accommodate loud or especially messy processes. Residents live alone on site. Selection by committee on strength of proposal, application, work samples and references. Virtual information session 21 July 2026, 1pm MT. Applicants notified September 2026. DEADLINE: 28 August 2026.

Pro Helvetia's Emerging Talents project extension grant supports extending advanced-stage design projects toward market success, for example through marketing, digital presence, and distribution. ELIGIBILITY: requires a connection to Switzerland (Swiss citizenship, or permanent residency with regular artistic activity in Switzerland); not open to practitioners without a Swiss connection. item.title: VSBfonds: Kunst & Cultuur Donations (rolling, Netherlands)
item.description:

Location: European Netherlands. Private legal entities (foundations, associations); applicants without a registered legal form are also eligible.

Award: No fixed minimum or maximum; the requested amount must be in proportion to other funding sources. No application fee.

Duration: Project funding; apply at least four months before the start date (two months for amateur arts initiatives).

Deadline: Rolling / undated

VSBfonds supports cultural initiatives that make it possible for everyone in the Netherlands to take part in art and culture, spanning ten programme lines from professional performances to community arts. Applications are accepted year-round with no deadlines from foundations, associations and applicants without a formal legal form, and must be submitted at least four months before the initiative starts (two months for amateur arts). A two-minute online quickscan checks eligibility before the formal application. No fixed minimum or maximum amount; the request should be proportionate to other funding. No application fee.

item.title: SIDN fonds: Pioneer Projects for a Strong Internet (rolling, Netherlands)
item.description:
Organisation: SIDN fonds

Location: Netherlands. Open to natural persons and legal entities for the pioneer track; theme calls require legal entities.

Award: Up to EUR 10,000 per pioneer project; theme calls (once or twice a year) fund larger projects above EUR 10,000. No application fee.

Duration: Pioneer projects develop an idea into a demo, pilot or experimental design; continuous intake.

Deadline: Rolling / undated

SIDN fonds (the foundation behind the .nl domain registry) invests in daring projects with societal added value that contribute to a strong internet and strong internet users. The Pioneers track is continuously open and awards up to EUR 10,000 to develop an innovative idea into a demo, pilot or experimental design; it is open to both individuals and legal entities. Larger projects are funded through theme calls issued once or twice a year (legal entities only). Projects must show innovation and public value and share their results openly; plain website or app building and purely B2B proposals are excluded. No application fee.
